gr-01-c2.text: Sean M. Carroll (1997). Lecture Notes on General Relativity. arXiv gr-qc/9712019 (Institute for Theoretical Physics, UC Santa Barbara).
gr-01-c2.quote: Once we have a metric, however, there is automatically a unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection.
gr-01-c2.claim: They're the connection coefficients of the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection, called the Levi-Civita connection, and they're computed entirely from the metric

gr-01-c3.text: Sean M. Carroll (1997). Lecture Notes on General Relativity. arXiv gr-qc/9712019 (Institute for Theoretical Physics, UC Santa Barbara).
gr-01-c3.quote: We have already argued, using the two-sphere as an example, that parallel transport of a vector around a closed loop in a curved space will lead to a transformation of the vector.
gr-01-c3.claim: Parallel transport around a closed loop measures curvature: carry a tangent vector around a small loop on a sphere and it comes back rotated.
